summary: Quilter is a leading UK wealth management business, providing financial planning advice and investment solutions. Formed from the UK and international business of Old Mutual Wealth, it was established as a standalone entity in 2018. The company manages investments on behalf of its clients, including affluent individuals and those approaching retirement, through a network of financial advisers. Quilter offers an integrated range of services encompassing financial advice, investment platforms, and multi-asset investment funds. It is known for its focus on the UK market and its comprehensive approach to helping clients plan for their financial future.

Millennium Management is a global multi-manager hedge fund founded in 1989, operating a platform of independent investment teams across asset classes and geographies. Headquartered in New York, the firm manages over $60 billion in assets and allocates capital to hundreds of portfolio managers running diverse, often uncorrelated strategies. Millennium is known for its robust risk management, proprietary infrastructure, and intense focus on performance and discipline. The firm operates offices across the US, Europe, and Asia, and competes with other multi-manager funds such as Citadel and Point72. With a highly selective hiring process and rigorous oversight model, Millennium continues to be one of the most sought-after and closely watched firms in the hedge fund industry.

Maven Securities is a proprietary trading firm based in London, specialising in options market-making and quantitative trading across global derivatives and equity markets. The firm operates on major exchanges in Europe, Asia, and the US, using advanced technology and data analytics to provide liquidity and capture short-term inefficiencies. Maven combines research, software development, and risk management in a flat, collaborative structure, attracting talent from both academia and industry. It trades a wide array of products, including ETFs, volatility instruments, and index options, and has a growing presence in crypto derivatives. The firm is known for its low-profile culture, fast-paced trading environment, and commitment to continuous improvement through experimentation and analysis.

Tower Research Capital is a quantitative trading firm founded in 1998, known for its high-frequency trading and market-making across global financial markets. Headquartered in New York with offices worldwide, Tower develops proprietary algorithms and low-latency systems to trade a wide range of asset classes, including equities, futures, and currencies. The firm employs teams of quantitative researchers, engineers, and traders who collaborate to build data-driven models and trading infrastructure. Tower is a prominent player in the electronic trading ecosystem and competes with other leading quant-driven firms for talent and speed.

Nvidia is a US-based technology company known for designing graphics processing units (GPUs) that power gaming, professional visualisation, and increasingly, AI and data centre workloads. Its hardware underpins a wide range of computing tasks—from rendering video games to training large language models—and its CUDA software ecosystem is central to high-performance computing. Nvidia has become one of the most valuable tech firms globally, driven by demand for AI chips and cloud infrastructure, and continues to expand into autonomous driving, robotics, and healthcare applications through both hardware and software development.

Monzo is a UK-based digital bank that offers personal and business banking services through a mobile-first platform. Launched in 2015, Monzo quickly gained traction with its intuitive app, real-time spending notifications, budgeting tools, and transparent fee structures. It has expanded into lending, savings, joint accounts, and paid subscription tiers, while also serving small businesses through Monzo Business. The bank operates under a full UK banking licence and has built a strong community-driven brand, especially among younger, digitally native users. Monzo is also active in open banking and fintech partnerships, positioning itself as a challenger to traditional high street banks with a focus on usability and customer service.

Allianz Insurance is part of the wider Allianz Group, one of the world’s largest providers of insurance and financial services. Headquartered in Germany and founded in 1890, it offers products across property, life, health, and business risk categories. Allianz serves both individuals and companies in more than 70 countries through local and global operations.

Police Scotland is the national police force of Scotland, responsible for maintaining law and order throughout the country. Formed in 2013 through the merger of eight regional police forces, it serves a population of over five million people. Police Scotland focuses on community policing, crime prevention, and responding to emergencies, working closely with local communities and other agencies to ensure public safety. The force aims to deliver a consistent and high-quality policing service across Scotland, addressing local needs while tackling national priorities.

BlackRock is the world’s largest asset manager, overseeing trillions in assets across index funds, ETFs, active strategies, and alternatives. Founded in 1988 and headquartered in New York, the firm serves institutional, corporate, and retail investors worldwide. Its product suite includes iShares, the world’s most widely used ETF platform, and Aladdin, its proprietary risk and portfolio management system. BlackRock plays a major role in global capital markets, with influence over long-term investment trends, ESG integration, and financial technology innovation.

FactSet is a US-based financial data and analytics provider serving investment professionals, asset managers, hedge funds, and corporate finance teams. Headquartered in Connecticut, FactSet offers a wide suite of tools for portfolio analysis, research, risk management, ESG integration, and financial modelling. The platform aggregates and integrates content from thousands of global sources, with proprietary datasets and deep customisation capabilities. FactSet’s software is widely used across front, middle, and back office functions, often integrated with Excel, trading systems, and client reporting tools. It has invested heavily in artificial intelligence, APIs, and open data architecture, allowing firms to build tailored investment workflows and automate insights. FactSet competes with larger incumbents like Bloomberg and Refinitiv, but is known for its nimble product development, transparent pricing, and strong customer service. It is increasingly positioning itself as a next-gen solution for data-driven investment processes.

Ithaca Energy is an independent oil and gas company focused on the acquisition, development, and production of hydrocarbon assets in the UK North Sea. Founded in 2004 and headquartered in Aberdeen, Scotland, the company has grown to become a significant operator in the region. Ithaca Energy is known for its substantial production volumes and its strategy of consolidating mature, high quality assets. It aims to maximize economic recovery from its portfolio, contributing to the UK's energy supply. The company is committed to operational efficiency and disciplined capital allocation to deliver stable cash flow and returns to its stakeholders.

Legal & General is a leading UK-based financial services group providing life insurance, pensions, investment management, and retirement solutions to individuals and institutions. Founded in 1836 and headquartered in London, the firm manages over £1 trillion in assets and is one of the UK’s largest investors in housing, infrastructure, and clean energy. Its investment management division, LGIM, is one of the world’s largest asset managers, known for passive strategies, ESG integration, and liability-driven investing. Legal & General also offers bulk annuities, lifetime mortgages, and workplace pensions, playing a key role in the UK’s financial system. With a strong focus on long-term social impact, the firm combines commercial scale with a commitment to inclusive capitalism and is active in policy discussions around retirement security and sustainable growth.

DV Trading is a multi-asset proprietary trading firm headquartered in Chicago, with additional offices in Toronto, London, and Singapore. The firm trades in global futures, options, fixed income, FX, and equities using a mix of quantitative models and discretionary execution. It supports its traders with in-house risk systems, technology infrastructure, and proprietary research tools. DV Trading is known for its agility, flat structure, and strong track record in volatile and fragmented markets, including energy and interest rate derivatives.

Aries Global is a London-based federation of founder-led software companies building an AI operating system for B2B SaaS. Launched in 2024 by former L Catterton and Snowflake EMEA leaders, the group unites niche cloud marketplace applications under one platform, investing over $100 million annually to acquire and scale vertical-focused enterprise software businesses with shared AI infrastructure.

Climate Policy Initiative is a global analysis and advisory organization that works to improve the effectiveness of climate and energy policy around the world. Founded in 2009, it provides independent, data-driven assessments of policy and finance issues. The organization focuses on identifying and promoting innovative solutions that drive the transition to a low carbon, climate resilient economy. CPI works with governments, businesses, and financial institutions to help them make better investment and policy decisions. It aims to bridge the gap between research and action in the climate finance space.

Giant Ventures is a venture capital firm that focuses on investing in early stage technology companies that aim to solve some of the world's most significant challenges. Founded in 2019 and based in London, the firm supports startups across sectors such as climate tech, digital health, and inclusive fintech. Giant Ventures is known for its mission driven approach and its commitment to backing founders who prioritize sustainable growth alongside positive societal impact. It leverages a global network of entrepreneurs and corporate leaders to provide strategic guidance and operational expertise to its portfolio companies.

Tesco is the UK’s largest grocery retailer and one of the leading retail groups in Europe, operating supermarkets, convenience stores, online grocery delivery, and wholesale services. Headquartered in Welwyn Garden City, Tesco serves millions of customers through its extensive store network and digital platforms. The company also offers banking and mobile services through Tesco Bank and Tesco Mobile. It is known for its customer loyalty programs, supply chain efficiency, and private-label products, and has made significant investments in sustainability, food waste reduction, and value-driven pricing across its business.

Quantum Dice is a UK-based quantum technology startup developing hardware-based random number generators using quantum mechanics. A spinout from the University of Oxford, the company focuses on enabling secure encryption and communication by generating truly unpredictable numbers in real time. Its Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) technology is designed for use in cybersecurity, finance, and defence, where high-assurance randomness is critical. Quantum Dice works closely with academic and industrial partners to integrate its solutions into secure chips, network infrastructure, and emerging quantum systems.

OakNorth is a UK-based commercial bank and fintech lender focused on supporting small and medium-sized businesses with tailored debt finance solutions. Founded in 2015, the bank leverages its proprietary credit intelligence platform to assess and monitor lending opportunities more dynamically than traditional banks. It offers loans typically ranging from £0.5m to £50m and has become a significant player in SME lending, serving a wide range of sectors including real estate, healthcare, hospitality, and manufacturing. OakNorth also licenses its credit technology to other financial institutions internationally, supporting better risk assessment and portfolio monitoring. It operates under a UK banking licence and combines a strong technology backbone with a relationship-driven service model, aiming to close the gap between small business credit demand and mainstream bank offerings.

Macquarie Group is a global financial services firm headquartered in Sydney, Australia, offering services across asset management, banking, commodities, and capital markets. Known for its entrepreneurial culture and decentralised structure, Macquarie operates through specialised groups that manage infrastructure, green energy, real estate, and credit investments worldwide. It is one of the world’s largest infrastructure asset managers and a major player in commodity trading and energy finance. The firm’s global advisory and capital markets division supports clients with M&A, equity, and debt financing, often with a focus on complex or cross-border transactions. Macquarie has expanded significantly in Europe and North America and is recognised for combining risk discipline with innovation across sectors including renewables, tech, and transportation.

MBDA is a European multinational defence company specialising in the design and production of missile systems and related technologies for air, land, and naval applications. Headquartered in France and jointly owned by Airbus, BAE Systems, and Leonardo, MBDA supplies guided weapons and air defence solutions to NATO members and allied nations. The company plays a central role in Europe’s defence industrial base, participating in major programmes such as the CAMM missile family, Storm Shadow, and Aster. MBDA also collaborates with national defence ministries on next-generation systems including hypersonic and counter-drone technologies. With R&D and manufacturing facilities in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Spain, it combines transnational cooperation with deep local engineering expertise.

Certara is a global biosimulation company accelerating drug development. It provides software and consulting services to pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, as well as regulatory agencies. Certara's technology helps predict how drugs will behave in the human body, optimizing clinical trial design and improving decision making. The company’s solutions span the drug development lifecycle, from early research to regulatory submissions.

NASDAQ is a leading global electronic marketplace for buying and selling securities, particularly known for listing technology and growth companies. Founded in 1971 and based in New York, it was the world’s first electronic stock market. NASDAQ operates several exchanges and provides market data, financial technology, and listing services to companies globally. It is recognised for its innovative trading technology, its role in facilitating capital formation, and its support for companies driving future economic growth. The platform offers a transparent and efficient environment for investors and issuers.

Squarepoint Capital is a global quantitative investment management firm that trades across a range of asset classes using systematic and data-driven strategies. With offices in New York, London, Singapore, and other financial hubs, Squarepoint operates in liquid markets across equities, FX, futures, and options. The firm integrates advanced analytics, proprietary algorithms, and scientific research into its trading and portfolio construction processes. Originally part of Barclays before spinning out in 2014, Squarepoint is known for its rigorous hiring standards, sophisticated technology stack, and focus on risk-adjusted returns across market cycles.

Figma is a cloud-native design platform founded in 2012, headquartered in San Francisco, and publicly traded under the ticker FIG. The company enables real-time, collaborative interface and product design through tools like Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides, and AI-enhanced workflows—all accessible via browser or desktop. Figma’s seamless collaboration across design teams, developers, and stakeholders has revolutionized how digital products are created.

American Express is a multinational financial services company best known for its charge cards, credit cards, and related payment solutions. Founded in 1850, the company evolved from freight forwarding into financial services and became a key player in travel, expense management, and consumer payments. Today, Amex operates across retail and commercial markets worldwide, with a strong emphasis on premium products, loyalty programmes, and high-spending customer segments. Its global merchant network and brand reputation make it a distinct competitor in the payments industry.

Cogna is a London-based AI startup transforming enterprise software with its natural-language platform that lets businesses generate custom applications in days, not months. Founded in 2023, Cogna serves sectors like utilities and infrastructure, enabling domain experts to define operational needs in plain English and receive precision tools without traditional coding or ERP customisation. Backed by investors including Notion and Hoxton Ventures, Cogna is redefining productivity for legacy industries through AI-driven automation.

Metrea is a US-based defence and aerospace company focused on delivering mission-critical services and technologies to government and military clients. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Washington, D.C., the firm provides capabilities across domains including airborne ISR (intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance), electronic warfare, secure communications, and tactical aviation. Metrea operates a fleet of modified aircraft and deploys proprietary systems in support of global defence missions, often as a private sector partner to NATO-aligned governments. The company follows a platform-based model, acquiring and integrating specialist defence service providers under a unified command and control structure. Metrea positions itself as a modern defence partner for contested environments and high-readiness operations.

DRW is a diversified proprietary trading firm headquartered in Chicago, operating at the intersection of trading, technology, and quantitative research. Founded in 1992, the firm trades across asset classes including fixed income, FX, equities, and digital assets, using both systematic and discretionary strategies. DRW also invests in financial market infrastructure and early-stage technologies through its venture arm. Known for its data-centric and collaborative culture, DRW has built a strong global presence in high-frequency and options trading.

Moloco is a leading machine learning company that provides programmatic advertising and monetization solutions for mobile businesses. Founded in 2013 and based in Redwood City, California, the company offers a robust platform for app developers and marketers to acquire users and maximize ad revenue. Moloco is known for its proprietary machine learning engine, which optimizes campaign performance through real time bidding and deep learning algorithms. It combines advanced data science with precise targeting capabilities, helping clients globally achieve significant growth and efficient ad spend.

MathWorks is a US-based software company best known for developing MATLAB and Simulink, widely used platforms for numerical computing, data analysis, and model-based design. Headquartered in Natick, Massachusetts, the firm serves engineers, researchers, and data scientists across industries including aerospace, automotive, finance, and academia. MATLAB is a standard tool for algorithm development, machine learning, and simulation, while Simulink supports system modelling for embedded and control systems. MathWorks is known for its technical excellence, strong academic ties, and focus on applied engineering problems, and continues to expand its offerings in AI, signal processing, and cloud-based development environments.

Nutanix is a US-based enterprise software company that provides cloud infrastructure solutions, helping businesses run applications and manage data across hybrid and multicloud environments. Its core platform enables customers to virtualise their IT infrastructure, replacing traditional data centres with flexible, software-defined systems. Nutanix is widely used by enterprises looking to modernise their operations without being locked into a single cloud provider. The company focuses on scalability, simplicity, and automation, with services that support everything from storage and networking to security and disaster recovery.

TPP (The Phoenix Partnership) is a Leeds-based healthcare technology company founded in 1997, best known for its flagship Electronic Health Record platform, SystmOne. It serves thousands of NHS organisations and clinicians across GP practices, hospitals, prisons, and mental health services, enabling secure and seamless access to patient data that improves care coordination and outcomes. Privately owned with no external shareholders, TPP fosters a mission-driven culture focused on supporting healthcare professionals and patients.

Wise, formerly known as TransferWise, is a UK-based financial technology company that enables low-cost, transparent international money transfers and multi-currency banking services. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in London, the company serves both individuals and businesses, allowing users to hold and convert over 50 currencies within a single account. Wise uses real exchange rates and low, upfront fees, positioning itself as an alternative to traditional banks for cross-border payments. The firm is publicly listed on the London Stock Exchange and continues to expand its services, including borderless accounts, business payment APIs, and card products. Wise is widely recognised for its mission-driven branding, customer loyalty, and product simplicity.

Thales is a French multinational company specialising in aerospace, defence, transportation, and digital security systems. Headquartered in Paris, the firm develops advanced technologies for avionics, radar, satellites, cybersecurity, and critical infrastructure protection. It serves governments, defence ministries, and large corporates with solutions in mission-critical systems and secure communications. Thales is also active in civil markets, including air traffic control and rail signalling, and is known for its investments in artificial intelligence, quantum technology, and digital identity. The company plays a major role in European defence and aerospace cooperation and is a key supplier to NATO and EU programs.

Copper.co is a London-based digital asset infrastructure provider offering custody, trading, and settlement solutions for institutional investors. Founded in 2018, the company enables secure access to over 500 digital assets through its proprietary platform. Copper’s technology includes MPC (multi-party computation) custody and ClearLoop, a system designed to mitigate counterparty risk during crypto trading. The firm serves asset managers, banks, and hedge funds, and has become a key player in institutional crypto infrastructure.

Rolls-Royce is a UK-based engineering company focused on power systems for aerospace, defence, and energy applications. Headquartered in Derby, the firm is best known for designing and manufacturing aircraft engines used in commercial and military aviation, and is one of the world’s leading engine suppliers. Beyond aerospace, Rolls-Royce develops propulsion systems for naval ships, small modular nuclear reactors, and industrial power solutions. The company is heavily invested in R&D, including sustainable aviation technologies and net-zero propulsion systems. It operates globally and plays a critical role in aerospace innovation, export manufacturing, and national defence capabilities.

AstraZeneca is a global, science-led biopharmaceutical company, specialising in the discovery, development, manufacturing, and commercialisation of prescription medicines. Formed in 1999 through the merger of Astra AB and Zeneca Group PLC and headquartered in Cambridge, UK, the company focuses on serious diseases across several therapeutic areas. AstraZeneca is known for its extensive research and development pipeline, innovative drug portfolio, and commitment to addressing unmet medical needs. It combines cutting-edge scientific research with a global commercial presence and has a track record of delivering life-changing medicines to patients worldwide.

Epic Games is a leading American video game and software developer, best known as the creator of Fortnite, one of the most successful video games of all time. Founded in 1991 and headquartered in Cary, North Carolina, the company also develops Unreal Engine, a widely used game development platform employed not only in gaming, but also in film, architecture, automotive design, and virtual production. Epic’s business spans game publishing, metaverse development, and online ecosystems, including the Epic Games Store. The company is known for its bold positioning in industry debates around platform economics and developer revenue sharing, often taking a vocal stance against traditional app store policies. With significant backing from Tencent and other investors, Epic continues to invest in building cross-platform tools and immersive digital experiences that shape the future of interactive media.

Castleton Commodities International (CCI) is a global trading and investment firm focused on energy and commodities markets. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, CCI trades physical and financial products across oil, natural gas, power, and metals. The firm also owns and operates energy infrastructure, including storage, transportation, and processing assets. CCI blends proprietary trading with strategic asset investment, and is known for its expertise in market fundamentals, logistics, and supply chain optimisation.

Frontier Economics is a leading economic consultancy headquartered in London, with additional offices across Europe and Australia. The firm advises corporates, regulators, governments, and international institutions on strategic, regulatory, and competition issues using rigorous economic analysis. Its work spans sectors such as energy, telecoms, financial services, healthcare, transport, and digital markets. Frontier is frequently called upon in antitrust cases, market investigations, and public policy evaluations, providing expert testimony and economic modelling. The firm is employee-owned and places a strong emphasis on independent thinking, intellectual curiosity, and transparency. Known for its high-calibre economists and clear communication of complex topics, Frontier plays a prominent role in shaping regulatory frameworks and major strategic decisions for both public and private clients.

Hacktron AI is an innovative technology firm dedicated to developing advanced artificial intelligence solutions for cybersecurity. It specializes in automated threat detection, vulnerability management, and predictive security analytics. Founded in 2018 and based in Palo Alto, the firm provides its cutting edge platforms to corporations, government entities, and IT service providers globally. Hacktron AI is known for its pioneering use of machine learning in defense strategies, its robust predictive capabilities, and its mission to secure digital infrastructures. It combines deep AI research with practical security applications, enabling organizations to proactively counter sophisticated cyber attacks and enhance their resilience.

Talos is a fintech platform that provides trading infrastructure for digital assets, enabling institutional investors to access crypto markets through a unified, secure interface. The platform offers order routing, execution, settlement, and portfolio management tools, and connects clients to exchanges, custodians, and liquidity providers. Talos serves hedge funds, banks, and asset managers looking to expand into digital assets while maintaining institutional-grade risk controls. The company is headquartered in New York and has become a core piece of market infrastructure in the growing institutional crypto ecosystem.

IMC Trading is a global market maker and proprietary trading firm based in Amsterdam, with major offices in Chicago, Sydney, and other financial centres. Founded in 1989, the firm uses sophisticated algorithms, low-latency infrastructure, and real-time data to provide liquidity across equities, ETFs, derivatives, and fixed income products on over 100 exchanges worldwide. IMC plays a critical role in financial markets by narrowing bid-ask spreads and ensuring efficient price discovery, competing with firms like Jane Street, Optiver, and Citadel Securities. It operates on a flat organisational structure and places strong emphasis on collaboration between traders, engineers, and quantitative researchers. Known for its rigorous recruitment and data-driven culture, IMC invests heavily in proprietary technology and trading systems, and actively participates in market structure discussions to help shape the future of global trading.

Man Group is a London-based active investment management firm with a global footprint, managing over $140 billion across strategies including hedge funds, long-only, and private markets. The firm operates through multiple investment engines—such as AHL, GLG, Numeric, and Man Global Private Markets—each with distinct styles, from quantitative and systematic to discretionary and fundamental. Man is especially recognised for its strength in data-driven strategies, risk management, and ESG integration, supported by in-house research and technology platforms. As a publicly listed asset manager, Man Group combines institutional scale with a multi-boutique model, offering customised solutions to pension funds, endowments, and wealth managers globally.

Mako is a proprietary trading and market-making firm based in London, with additional offices in Amsterdam, Singapore, and Sydney. The firm specialises in options, ETFs, fixed income, and digital assets, operating across global exchanges with a focus on liquidity provision and risk-neutral strategies. Founded in 1999, Mako blends quantitative research, cutting-edge technology, and trader expertise to capture opportunities in complex and fast-moving markets. It maintains a low-profile culture, with an emphasis on collaboration and long-term growth rather than high-frequency competition. The firm also supports a number of initiatives in education and technology through its philanthropic and venture arms.

SLB, formerly Schlumberger, is one of the world’s largest oilfield services companies, providing technology and services across the exploration, drilling, and production lifecycle. Headquartered in Houston, Paris, London, and The Hague, SLB serves major energy producers globally and has expanded into digital, carbon management, and new energy systems such as geothermal and hydrogen. The firm develops advanced tools for subsurface analysis, well construction, and reservoir engineering, and is increasingly focused on decarbonisation solutions. SLB is central to upstream oil and gas operations and plays a growing role in the energy transition through its New Energy division.

Jane Street is a global proprietary trading firm and liquidity provider known for its expertise in quantitative trading, technology development, and financial engineering. Headquartered in New York with offices in London, Hong Kong, and Amsterdam, the firm trades a wide array of asset classes—including equities, ETFs, options, fixed income, and crypto—across both traditional and electronic markets. Jane Street combines rigorous mathematical research with cutting-edge software development, operating in a highly collaborative, flat organisational structure. It is a major player in ETF market making and provides liquidity to markets around the clock, contributing to efficiency and price discovery. The firm is known for its analytical culture, competitive hiring process, and deep investment in proprietary systems and infrastructure. Jane Street remains privately held and low-profile, but plays an outsized role in global financial markets, particularly in electronic and algorithmic trading.

Siemens is a German multinational industrial and technology company operating across automation, digital industries, smart infrastructure, healthcare (via Siemens Healthineers), and mobility. Headquartered in Munich, the firm has a long history of innovation in electrification, manufacturing systems, and industrial software. Siemens plays a central role in digital transformation across industries, offering solutions that combine hardware, AI, and cloud connectivity. The company also develops railway systems, imaging diagnostics, and energy efficiency technologies, with a growing focus on sustainability, decarbonisation, and the digitalisation of critical infrastructure.

Wincent is a London-based private investment firm focused on long-term partnerships with high-growth businesses in Europe and beyond. The firm provides flexible capital solutions, often through minority investments, to founder-led or entrepreneur-driven companies across sectors including technology, consumer, healthcare, and business services. Wincent distinguishes itself by avoiding a rigid fund structure, enabling it to take a patient, collaborative approach without exit pressure. The firm typically supports its portfolio companies with strategic input, growth planning, and network access, while allowing management teams to retain operational control. It aims to align closely with founders' goals and business values over time.

UiPath is a global software company specializing in Robotic Process Automation, providing an end-to-end platform for automating business processes. Founded in 2005 and headquartered in New York, the company serves enterprises worldwide, enabling them to streamline operations through intelligent automation. UiPath's platform combines artificial intelligence with a visual development environment, allowing organizations to deploy software robots that mimic human actions. It is known for driving digital transformation, improving operational efficiency, and enhancing productivity across various industries.

Multus is a biotechnology company focused on the development of high performance, affordable growth media for the cultivated meat industry. Founded in 2019 and based in London, the company aims to accelerate the transition to sustainable food production by replacing animal derived components with cost effective alternatives. Multus provides essential ingredients that allow cellular agriculture producers to scale their manufacturing processes while maintaining strict quality standards. By optimizing the biological inputs necessary for cell growth, the firm supports the development of commercially viable, lab grown protein products for the global market.

role: Summer Internship - Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
summary: Mewburn Ellis is a leading intellectual property firm, specialising in patents, trademarks, designs, and copyright. Founded in 1872 and based in the UK, the firm advises a diverse client base including startups, universities, and multinational corporations. Mewburn Ellis is known for its long history, deep technical expertise, and strategic approach to IP protection and management. It combines legal prowess with commercial understanding, offering comprehensive support for innovation across various sectors.

CommonAI CIC is a UK based company focusing on artificial intelligence for the common good. They operate as a community interest company, meaning their profits are reinvested into their social mission. CommonAI CIC aims to promote the ethical development and application of AI technologies. They work on projects related to healthcare, environmental sustainability, and education, collaborating with researchers, policymakers, and community organizations.

Redgate is a UK-based software company that develops tools for database management, primarily for Microsoft SQL Server and other relational databases. Headquartered in Cambridge, it serves developers and IT teams with solutions for DevOps, data privacy, monitoring, and deployment automation. Redgate’s tools are widely used by enterprise clients to improve collaboration between developers and database administrators, reduce errors, and ensure compliance in complex environments. The company has built a loyal user base through its focus on simplicity, developer experience, and continuous product innovation, particularly in highly regulated sectors such as finance and healthcare.

Microsoft is one of the world’s largest technology companies, offering software, hardware, cloud services, and enterprise solutions across a broad spectrum of industries. Headquartered in Redmond, Washington, the company is best known for products like Windows, Office, Azure, LinkedIn, and Xbox. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has transformed into a cloud-first, subscription-based business, with Azure becoming a cornerstone of its growth strategy in infrastructure-as-a-service and AI applications. Microsoft serves consumers, businesses, and governments, and is a key player in digital transformation, cybersecurity, and productivity tools. The firm is also actively involved in open-source development, sustainability initiatives, and accessibility, and remains one of the most valuable and influential companies in the global tech ecosystem.

AVEVA is a UK-based industrial software company that provides engineering and operations solutions to firms across energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, and marine sectors. Founded in 1967 as a spin-out from the University of Cambridge, AVEVA has evolved into a global leader in digital twin technology, asset lifecycle management, and process simulation. Its software helps industrial clients improve operational efficiency, reduce downtime, and transition toward more sustainable practices. AVEVA became part of the Schneider Electric Group in 2023, strengthening its position in industrial digital transformation.

Meta Platforms, formerly Facebook Inc., is a US-based technology conglomerate known for its social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, as well as its investments in virtual reality, AI, and digital infrastructure. Headquartered in Menlo Park, California, Meta plays a central role in the global digital economy, monetising user engagement through targeted advertising while also investing heavily in the development of the metaverse through its Reality Labs division. The company has pivoted toward immersive digital experiences, including AR/VR, 3D environments, and wearable tech. Despite facing scrutiny over data privacy and platform moderation, Meta remains one of the most influential firms in tech, shaping communication, media, and digital interaction for billions of users worldwide.

Jump Trading is a proprietary trading firm and technology company based in Chicago, known for its expertise in algorithmic and high-frequency trading across global financial markets. Founded in 1999, the firm trades a broad range of asset classes including equities, fixed income, futures, options, and cryptocurrencies, operating on over 100 exchanges worldwide. Jump places a strong emphasis on quantitative research, advanced hardware and software development, and low-latency infrastructure, competing with firms such as DRW, Citadel Securities, and Jane Street. It is also involved in crypto through Jump Crypto, a dedicated division focused on trading, venture investments, and protocol development. The firm is privately held and secretive, known for its flat structure, highly selective hiring, and deep investment in proprietary technology and applied science.

NCR Atleos is a global technology company that provides solutions for the financial, retail, and hospitality industries. The company is a leading provider of ATMs, point-of-sale systems, and self-service kiosks. NCR Atleos also offers a range of software and services to help businesses manage their operations and improve the customer experience. The company has a long history of innovation and is committed to developing new technologies that meet the evolving needs of its customers.

OneStream provides a unified corporate performance management platform that streamlines financial consolidation, planning, reporting, analytics, and data quality. Headquartered in Rochester, Michigan, the company serves various industries, offering solutions that integrate financial and operational data into a single, extensible platform. OneStream is known for its scalability, flexibility, and ability to handle complex business requirements, helping organizations improve decision-making and gain better insights into their performance.

The Financial Conduct Authority is the UK’s primary regulator for financial markets and services, responsible for protecting consumers, ensuring market integrity, and promoting competition. Based in London, the FCA regulates nearly 50,000 firms, including banks, insurers, asset managers, and fintechs. It oversees a wide array of sectors from retail lending and advice to trading platforms, cryptoassets, and listing requirements. The FCA sets conduct standards, monitors systemic risks, enforces rules through investigations and fines, and develops regulatory policy in line with market developments and government objectives. It works closely with the Bank of England, PRA, and international bodies like ESMA and IOSCO. The FCA has taken a leading role on issues such as green finance, digital assets, operational resilience, and financial inclusion, and continues to evolve its supervisory approach to address technological innovation and post-Brexit regulation.

PQShield is a UK-based cybersecurity company specialising in post-quantum cryptography, helping organisations future-proof their data and systems against the threat of quantum computing. A spinout from the University of Oxford, PQShield develops cryptographic solutions for hardware, software, and communications — including secure messaging, chip-level encryption, and enterprise-level protocols. The company works with governments, defence contractors, and multinational technology firms to integrate quantum-resistant cryptographic standards. PQShield is a contributor to global standard-setting bodies such as NIST and is regarded as a key player in preparing cybersecurity infrastructure for the post-quantum era.

SPAICE is a technology company developing the Autonomy Operating System, designed to empower satellites and drones to navigate, perceive, and interact with their surroundings in any environment. Its Spatial AI enables full autonomy, resilience, and adaptability - from GPS-denied zones on Earth to deep-space missions. The company collaborates with leading aerospace and defense contractors to deliver real-world impact, driving the next generation of intelligent, autonomous systems that operate beyond traditional limits.

UBS is a global financial services firm headquartered in Zurich, offering wealth management, investment banking, asset management, and retail banking. With a particularly strong presence in global wealth management, UBS serves high-net-worth and institutional clients across Europe, the Americas, and Asia-Pacific. The firm also operates a sizeable investment banking division and is active in advisory, capital markets, and equities trading. UBS has placed increased emphasis on sustainable investing, digital innovation, and its integrated client model following its 2023 acquisition of Credit Suisse, reshaping the landscape of European banking.

American Express is a multinational financial services company best known for its charge cards, credit cards, and related payment solutions. Founded in 1850, the company evolved from freight forwarding into financial services and became a key player in travel, expense management, and consumer payments. Today, Amex operates across retail and commercial markets worldwide, with a strong emphasis on premium products, loyalty programmes, and high-spending customer segments. Its global merchant network and brand reputation make it a distinct competitor in the payments industry.

role: 2027 Summer Internship – Data Engineer, Long/Short Equities
summary: Point72 is a global asset management firm founded by Steven A. Cohen in 2014, following the transition from SAC Capital. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, the firm manages capital across multiple strategies including long/short equity, macro, systematic, and private investments. Its discretionary investing teams operate with autonomy within a multi-manager platform, while its Cubist division focuses on quantitative and algorithmic trading. Point72 also runs a venture capital arm, Point72 Ventures, investing in fintech, healthcare, and enterprise technology. With offices in major financial centres including New York, London, Tokyo, and Singapore, the firm is known for its strong emphasis on data, technology, and talent development, particularly through its structured analyst training programs like the Point72 Academy.

Direct Soccer is a major online retailer of football teamwear, equipment, and accessories in the UK. The company supplies clubs, schools, and individual players with a wide range of products, including jerseys, training gear, and footballs. Direct Soccer is known for its competitive pricing, extensive product selection, and customization services like shirt printing and embroidery. They focus on providing a convenient and comprehensive solution for football teams and players at all levels.

Parexel is a leading global Contract Research Organization (CRO) providing a comprehensive suite of clinical research and development services. Founded in 1982 and headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, the company supports pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies worldwide. Parexel is known for its extensive expertise across various therapeutic areas and its integrated solutions, spanning from early phase clinical development through regulatory affairs and market access. It focuses on accelerating the delivery of innovative therapies to patients globally by combining deep scientific and clinical capabilities with advanced technology.

Dow Jones is a leading provider of global business news, financial information, and data analytics, best known for publishing The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, and MarketWatch. Owned by News Corp, the company also delivers data-driven products for compliance, risk, and research through platforms like Factiva and Dow Jones Risk & Compliance. Its editorial and data offerings serve a wide range of audiences, from consumers to global financial institutions. Dow Jones is synonymous with business journalism and continues to shape financial media and market intelligence.

Expedia Group is a global online travel and technology company that owns and operates a portfolio of brands including Expedia.com, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Trivago, and Egencia. Headquartered in Seattle, the group provides services across flight bookings, hotel reservations, car rentals, vacation rentals, and corporate travel solutions. Expedia operates a dual-sided marketplace, connecting consumers with travel suppliers such as airlines and hoteliers, while offering tools for dynamic pricing, inventory management, and customer engagement. The company is heavily invested in artificial intelligence and personalisation technologies to enhance user experience and optimise search and recommendations. It is also focused on sustainability and loyalty initiatives, offering the One Key rewards programme across multiple platforms. Expedia plays a central role in the digital transformation of global travel and continues to evolve as a travel-tech ecosystem provider.

Tencent is one of China’s largest technology conglomerates, operating across digital entertainment, social platforms, fintech, and cloud computing. Headquartered in Shenzhen, Tencent owns WeChat and QQ, and is a major player in gaming through titles like Honor of Kings and its stake in global studios such as Riot Games and Epic Games. The company also has a large venture and investment arm, with holdings in e-commerce, AI, and software businesses worldwide. Tencent’s business model blends platform ecosystems with content and services, and it continues to expand into international markets while navigating regulatory pressures in China.

EY is one of the Big Four professional services firms, offering audit, tax, consulting, and transaction advisory services to clients around the world. Headquartered in London and operating in over 150 countries, EY serves governments, corporations, and financial institutions across industries including tech, healthcare, finance, and energy. The firm is structured as a global network of member firms and employs over 300,000 people. EY is known for its strengths in assurance and deal advisory, as well as its fast-growing consulting business, which supports clients on digital transformation, ESG strategy, and cyber risk. The firm invests heavily in innovation, including its proprietary AI and analytics platforms, and has made bold moves to modernise its business model—most notably exploring the separation of audit and consulting. EY also plays a leadership role in sustainability reporting and inclusive leadership development through initiatives like EY Ripples.

Crédit Agricole is one of the largest banking groups in Europe and a major player in retail, corporate, and investment banking. Headquartered in France, the group includes a network of regional cooperative banks as well as specialised subsidiaries offering services in asset management, insurance, leasing, and private banking. Crédit Agricole is a leader in green finance and responsible investing, and it supports clients across Europe and internationally with a strong presence in agriculture, infrastructure, and export financing.

Symphony is a secure communication and workflow platform built for financial institutions and regulated industries. Headquartered in New York, the firm offers encrypted messaging, collaboration, and automation tools for trading desks, operations teams, and compliance departments. Used by many of the world’s largest banks and asset managers, Symphony integrates with third-party applications and supports real-time data sharing in a secure environment. It plays a central role in digitising communication in capital markets while meeting regulatory and cybersecurity standards.

Leonardo is an Italian multinational aerospace, defence, and security company headquartered in Rome, operating across sectors including helicopters, electronics, space, and military aircraft. Formerly known as Finmeccanica, the firm is partially owned by the Italian government and serves both domestic and international defence markets. Leonardo designs and manufactures advanced systems for air, land, sea, and cyber applications, and is a key partner in European defence collaboration programmes including Eurofighter Typhoon and the GCAP fighter initiative. The company also has a presence in civil aerospace, unmanned systems, and satellite communications, and has made strategic investments in digitalisation and AI-driven defence technologies. With a global industrial footprint and integrated supply chains, Leonardo is one of the top defence contractors in Europe and a major player in global aerospace innovation.

Brevan Howard is a global alternative investment management firm known for its expertise in macro trading and discretionary strategies. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Jersey, the firm manages capital on behalf of institutional investors across hedge funds, liquid alternatives, and digital asset strategies. Brevan Howard has offices in major financial centres including London, Geneva, New York, and Abu Dhabi. Its trading teams operate with significant autonomy, using macroeconomic and market research to make directional and relative value bets across asset classes.

Salesforce is a global cloud software company best known for its customer relationship management (CRM) platform, which helps businesses manage sales, service, marketing, and data integration. Headquartered in San Francisco, Salesforce is one of the largest enterprise software providers in the world, with a strong presence in AI, analytics, and workflow automation. Its platform includes products such as Sales Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and Tableau, and it has expanded through acquisitions including Slack and MuleSoft. The company is also recognised for its commitment to sustainability, philanthropy, and corporate activism, and continues to shape the future of digital enterprise infrastructure.

Bending Spoons is a Milan-based technology company focused on developing mobile apps and digital products across health, creativity, and productivity. Founded in 2013, the company has become one of Europe’s top app developers by global downloads. Its portfolio includes widely used apps for photo editing, fitness, document scanning, and AI-enhanced tools. Bending Spoons is known for its high standards in product design, in-house engineering, and a culture that emphasises innovation and speed.

Perplexity is an AI-powered search engine that provides direct answers to user queries using natural language processing. Founded in 2022, it combines search and large language models to offer concise summaries with source citations. Perplexity aims to provide comprehensive and transparent information retrieval, distinguishing itself from traditional search engines with its focus on conversational interaction and knowledge synthesis. The platform is designed to enhance research and information discovery by offering quick and accurate answers.

TTP is a UK-based technology and product development company that works with clients across life sciences, communications, and industrial sectors. Headquartered near Cambridge, TTP provides R&D, engineering, and design services to develop new products, platforms, and technologies — from diagnostics and medical devices to wireless systems and automation tools. The firm operates on a consultancy model, helping clients bring innovations from concept to market while maintaining in-house labs and prototyping capabilities. It is known for its multidisciplinary teams and ability to solve complex, technical challenges across high-impact sectors.
Convergent is an AI, world models and analytics platform to unlock human socio-cognitive potential, starting from high-stakes human interactions and decision-making in business and beyond.

PGIM is the global investment management business of Prudential Financial, managing more than $1.2 trillion in assets across public and private markets. Headquartered in Newark, New Jersey, PGIM operates through specialised affiliates including PGIM Fixed Income, PGIM Real Estate, and Jennison Associates, each with its own investment expertise. The firm serves institutional and retail clients worldwide, offering strategies in fixed income, equities, real estate, private credit, and alternatives. PGIM is known for its scale, long-term thinking, and research-led approach to managing portfolios in both traditional and less liquid markets.

HubSpot is a US-based software company providing a suite of inbound marketing, sales, customer service, and CRM tools aimed at helping businesses grow and manage customer relationships. Headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and founded in 2006, HubSpot pioneered the concept of inbound marketing—focusing on content-driven lead generation rather than traditional advertising—and has since expanded its platform into an all-in-one customer growth engine for SMEs and mid-market businesses. The company’s software includes marketing automation, CMS, email, CRM, customer support, and operations hubs, all designed to integrate seamlessly and scale with growing companies. HubSpot’s freemium model and strong community engagement have helped it become a category leader, and its products are used by over 100,000 customers globally. It is also known for its transparent company culture and thought leadership in sales enablement, customer success, and digital marketing.

Aquatic Capital Management is a Chicago-based quantitative investment firm specializing in systematic strategies that combine rigorous quantitative research, robust software engineering, and disciplined risk management to generate consistent, repeatable returns. Registered with the SEC and CFTC and managing approximately $5.5 billion in assets as of March 2024, the firm advises private funds grouped into structured “master/feeder” models and employs a unified, collaborative approach to trading.

Capgemini is a global consulting and IT services firm headquartered in Paris, offering services in strategy, technology, and digital transformation. Founded in 1967, the company operates in over 50 countries, delivering solutions in cloud computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and enterprise applications. Capgemini works with corporates, governments, and public institutions across industries, helping clients modernise legacy systems, streamline operations, and adopt new technologies. It also owns Capgemini Invent, a consulting unit focused on innovation and business design.

Gearset is a UK-based DevOps platform purpose-built for Salesforce development teams, offering tools to automate deployments, track changes, and manage version control in complex Salesforce environments. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge, Gearset has quickly become a market leader in Salesforce DevOps, trusted by enterprises, consultancies, and NGOs to improve release cycles and reduce deployment errors. The platform supports CI/CD pipelines, backup and recovery, sandbox management, and compliance monitoring, helping teams scale their Salesforce development while meeting governance standards. Gearset integrates with tools like GitHub, Jira, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps, enabling seamless collaboration across technical and business users. It’s widely praised for its user-friendly interface, responsive support, and robust documentation—making it a go-to choice for development teams working within the Salesforce ecosystem.

Runna is a digital running coach platform that offers personalized training plans and expert guidance. Founded in 2021 and based in London, the app caters to runners of all levels, from beginners to experienced marathoners, preparing for various race distances. Runna is known for its adaptive workout schedules, audio guided runs, and community features, making elite coaching accessible through technology. It combines data driven insights with practical support, helping users achieve their running goals and improve performance.

TE Connectivity is a global industrial technology company that designs and manufactures connectors, sensors, and electronic components for a wide range of industries. Headquartered in Switzerland, the firm serves sectors such as automotive, aerospace, medical, data communications, and industrial automation. TE Connectivity plays a critical role in enabling connectivity and signal integrity in harsh environments, supporting trends like electrification, autonomous systems, and smart infrastructure. The company combines advanced engineering with large-scale manufacturing and continues to expand its role in high-growth markets including EVs and industrial IoT.

Oxford Nanopore Technologies is a UK-based biotechnology company developing real-time DNA and RNA sequencing technologies. Spun out of the University of Oxford, the firm has pioneered portable and scalable sequencing devices that allow for on-site genetic analysis across clinical, research, and field settings. Its products, such as the MinION and PromethION, are used in applications ranging from infectious disease monitoring to agricultural genomics and personalised medicine. Oxford Nanopore differentiates itself through its nanopore-based approach, which enables long-read sequencing and flexibility in sample size and location. The company is listed on the London Stock Exchange and continues to expand its presence in diagnostics, healthcare, and research infrastructure.

Cirrus Logic is a fabless semiconductor supplier, specializing in high-precision analog and mixed-signal processing solutions. The company's products are used in a variety of audio and energy applications. Cirrus Logic focuses on designing and marketing integrated circuits for audio entertainment and energy efficiency. The company is headquartered in Austin, Texas, and operates worldwide, delivering technologies for smartphones, laptops, and automotive entertainment systems.

Keysight Technologies is a leading technology company providing electronic design and test solutions. Spun off from Agilent Technologies in 2014 and headquartered in Santa Rosa, California, the company serves engineers developing new products in sectors like aerospace, defense, automotive, and telecommunications. Keysight is recognized for its expertise in measurement science, offering hardware and software that accelerate innovation from design simulation to manufacturing test. It helps customers bring products to market faster and at lower cost.

The Trade Desk is a US-based technology company that operates a digital advertising platform enabling media buyers to plan, execute, and optimise programmatic ad campaigns across channels. Headquartered in California, its platform supports display, video, audio, native, and connected TV advertising, with a strong focus on data-driven targeting and measurement. The Trade Desk is widely used by agencies and brands seeking transparency and control over their digital ad spend, and has positioned itself as a key player in the shift away from walled garden platforms. It continues to invest in AI, identity resolution, and open internet infrastructure.
